CUMIN LAMB-STUFFED BELL PEPPERS

I have made this on more weeknights than I can count, and that’s
pecause my whole family will eat it without a single complaint. It looks
like far more effort than it takes, and the smoky lamb tastes
better the next day, if you can manage to keep any back. The sweet
peppers do most of the work for you.

MAKE THE PEPPERS Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a large
baking sheet with parchment paper.
Slice the tops off the peppers, halve them lengthwise, and pull
out the ribs. Set the peppers cut-side up on the baking sheet
and rub the insides with olive oil. Sprinkle with salt,
pepper, and paprika. Roast until the peppers slump and
soften, 20 to 25 minutes.

MAKE THE SPICED LAMB Warm the olive oil in a wide skillet over
medium-high heat until it ripples. Add the ground lamb, onion,
salt, and pepper and cook, pressing the meat apart with the edge
ofa spatula, until it has browned, 6 to 7 minutes. Spoon off any
extra fat.
Lower the heat to medium and add the ginger and garlic.
Cook until you can smell them, 1to 2 minutes. Add the drained
chopped tomatoes, cumin, coriander, and chile flakes and
stir to combine, Pour in the stock and simmer until it is gone, about
© Taste and add more salt and/or chile, if you like.
€Move the pan off the heat, cover, and hold it there until the
Peppers are ready,
Divide the meat mixture between the peppers, packing the
i :
Lamb
atin each one. Top each with the mint and serve.
